# Benchmarked performance (Vulkan vs ROCm vs CPU):
#   - Vulkan: ~800 tok/s prompt, ~40 tok/s generation (WINNER)
#   - ROCm:   ~30 tok/s prompt,  ~29 tok/s generation
#   - CPU:    ~28 tok/s prompt,  ~28 tok/s generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Mount points - LLM models on ZFS tank for unlimited storage
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/llm-models"
      volume = "/tank/llm-models"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with llama.cpp backend (Vulkan GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "llama-server", port = 8080, info = "LLM backend (Vulkan GPU)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) via Vulkan/RADV:
- `/dev/dri` device passthrough
- ~40 tok/s generation, ~800 tok/s prompt processing

**Check GPU detection:**
```
docker logs llama-server 2>&1 | grep -i vulkan
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f llama-server
```

**Test inference:**
```
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3.2-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```

**Download new model (GGUF format):**
```
cd /config/models
curl -L -O "https://huggingface.co/bartowski/MODEL/resolve/main/MODEL.gguf"
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "llama-cpp", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "openwebui_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    webui_secret_key    = random_password.openwebui_secret_key.result
    oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.openwebui.client_id
    oauth_client_secret = random_password.openwebui_oidc_secret.result
    openid_provider_url = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/openwebui/.well-known/openid-configuration"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/openwebui.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "openwebui_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.openwebui_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.openwebui.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.openwebui.container_id
  container_ip   = module.openwebui.ip_address
  container_name = "openwebui"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-501"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database dump needed - SQLite file backup is sufficient

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2", "/config/models/**"]  # Exclude GGUF models (can be re-downloaded)

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,openwebui"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenWebUI (AI Chat Interface)
module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal and public routes (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "ai.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# llama.cpp API (LLM Backend - OpenAI compatible)
module "llama_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "llama"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal only (OpenAI-compatible API access)
  internal_domain = "llama.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Basic auth for API access
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "llama-auth"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    openwebui = {
      internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
      public   = module.openwebui_route.public_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
    }
    llama = {
      internal = module.llama_route.internal_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"
    }
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    openwebui = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
    llama     = module.llama_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

   - No native Ollama API in llama.cpp
   - Both support OpenAI-compatible APIs (`/v1/chat/completions`)
   - LiteLLM could act as a translation layer
   - Recommended starting with llama.cpp native since OpenAI API is the common standard

3. **User chose native llama.cpp** over LiteLLM for simplicity

4. **Hardware Discovery**: Found user has AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) in LXC 501 with ROCm via `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0` workaround. Current Ollama config uses ROCm.

5. **Benchmarking Phase**:
   - Tested current Ollama GPU vs CPU
   - Results showed GPU (~28 tok/s) wasn't faster than CPU (~27 tok/s)
   - The HSA_OVERRIDE workaround wasn't providing real acceleration

6. **Research on ROCm 7.10**: Found ROCm 7.10 (Dec 2025) officially supports gfx1150 Strix Point APUs. Also found Vulkan (RADV) has 13% improvements in Mesa 25.3.

7. **User wanted to test both Vulkan and ROCm** - chose to test one at a time

8. **Created test docker-compose** with profiles for ROCm, Vulkan, and CPU backends

9. **Benchmark Results**:
   - ROCm 7.0: ~29-30 tok/s (same as CPU)
   - **Vulkan: ~37-42 tok/s generation, ~600-850 tok/s prompt** (CLEAR WINNER)
   - CPU: ~27-30 tok/s

10. **User approved switching to Vulkan**

11. **Updated Terraform files**:
    - `docker-compose.yml` - replaced Ollama with llama.cpp Vulkan
    - `main.tf` - updated descriptions, routes, notes
    - `common.yml` (Traefik) - renamed ollama-auth to llama-auth

12. **First apply failed** - model file didn't exist in `/config/models`

13. **Downloaded model** to `/config/models` and restarted

14. **User asked about storage** - 34GB on root disk, but models could get large. User has `/tank` ZFS pool with ~58TB available.

15. **User pointed out I didn't add mount_points via Terraform** - I had created the directory but forgot to add it to the module configuration.

16. **Fixed by adding mount_points** to main.tf:
    ```
    mount_points = [
      {
        slot   = 0
        path   = "/llm-models"
        volume = "/tank/llm-models"
      }
    ]
    ```

17. **Updated docker-compose** to use `/llm-models:/models` instead of `./models:/models`

18. **Downloaded model to tank** storage on Proxmox host

content.text:
Migration complete. All changes have been committed and pushed.

## Summary

Successfully migrated OpenWebUI from Ollama to llama.cpp with Vulkan GPU acceleration:

**Performance Results:**
- **Vulkan**: ~40 tok/s generation, ~800 tok/s prompt processing ✓
- ROCm: ~29 tok/s (same as CPU)
- CPU: ~28 tok/s

**Changes Made:**
- Replaced Ollama with `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan`
- Added ZFS mount (`/tank/llm-models` → `/llm-models`) for model storage
- Updated Traefik middleware from `ollama-auth` to `llama-auth`
- Cleaned up 12GB of old Ollama models
- Removed old `ollama.yml` Traefik route

**Connecting OpenWebUI to llama.cpp:**

OpenWebUI is already configured to connect via the OpenAI-compatible API. The key environment variables in [docker-compose.yml](tofu/apps/openwebui/deploy/docker-compose.yml#L10-L12):

```yaml
- OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://llama-server:8080/v1
- OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed
- ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false
```

The containers communicate via Docker networking - OpenWebUI reaches llama-server on port 8080 using the OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. The `depends_on` with health check ensures llama-server is ready before OpenWebUI starts.

**URLs:**
- OpenWebUI: `https://ai.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- llama.cpp API (internal): `https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev`

OpenWebUI is already configured to connect to llama.cpp. The connection is set up in [docker-compose.yml:10-12](tofu/apps/openwebui/deploy/docker-compose.yml#L10-L12):

```yaml
- OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://llama-server:8080/v1
- OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed
- ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false
```

**How it works:**

1. **Docker networking** - Both containers are in the same compose stack, so OpenWebUI reaches llama-server by container name
2. **OpenAI-compatible API** - llama.cpp exposes `/v1/chat/completions` which OpenWebUI natively supports
3. **Health check dependency** - OpenWebUI waits for llama-server to be healthy before starting

**To verify it's working:**

```bash
# Check containers are healthy
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "docker ps"

# Test the API directly
ssh root@10.100.5.101 'curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"llama-3.2-3b\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hi\"}]}" | jq -r .choices[0].message.content'
```

**To add a new model:**

1. Download a GGUF file to `/tank/llm-models` on Proxmox
2. Update `LLAMA_ARG_MODEL` in docker-compose.yml to point to the new model
3. Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui`

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Docker Socket Proxy - Secure Docker API access
  # ==========================================================================
  # Provides a filtered API proxy to Docker socket for security
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:v0.4.2
    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      # Container management
      - CONTAINERS=1
      - EXEC=1
      - IMAGES=1
      - NETWORKS=1
      - VOLUMES=1
      - POST=1
      # Status/info
      - EVENTS=1
      - PING=1
      - VERSION=1
      - INFO=1
      # Security: disable sensitive endpoints
      - AUTH=0
      - SECRETS=0
    networks:
      - internal
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.1'
        reservations:
          memory: 32m
          cpus: '0.05'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:2375/version || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # v5.0 adds AI-powered monitoring with Ollama integration.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:v5.0.2
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
    volumes:
      - ./pulse:/data
    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7655/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Arcane - Docker Container Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Modern Docker management UI with update detection.
  # Manages containers via remote agents on other LXCs.
  arcane:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:v1.11.0
    container_name: arcane
    ports:
      - "3552:3552"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - APP_URL=https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
      - ENCRYPTION_KEY=${ARCANE_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - JWT_SECRET=${ARCANE_JWT_SECRET}
    volumes:
      - arcane_data:/app/data
    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3552/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

networks:
  internal:
    internal: true

volumes:
  arcane_data:

module "llama_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "llama"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal only (OpenAI-compatible API access)
  internal_domain = "llama.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Middlewares - Basic auth for API access
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "llama-auth"]
}
```

**Available endpoints:**

| Access | URL | Auth |
|--------|-----|------|
| Internal (Traefik) | `https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev/v1` | Basic auth (`llama-api:<password>`) |
| Direct | `http://10.100.5.101:8080/v1` | None |

For **n8n** and other internal apps, you can use either:
- **Direct**: `http://10.100.5.101:8080/v1` (no auth needed, container network only)
- **Traefik**: `https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev/v1` (requires basic auth)

The direct URL is simpler for internal services. The Traefik route is useful if you want to access the API from your laptop or external tools with authentication.

The Pulse volume (`./pulse:/data`) contains runtime state that gets generated and updated. Syncing this back to the deploy directory would:

1. **Overwrite on next deploy** - The terraform deploy will sync local → container, potentially losing current state
2. **Include sensitive runtime data** - API tokens, sessions, encryption keys

**What should happen:**
- The deploy directory should be minimal or empty for Pulse (just initial config if needed)
- Runtime state should stay in the container volume and be backed up via PBS

2. **Pull current state from container** - Sync container → local (not recommended, as it includes runtime secrets)
3. **Add pulse to exclude_patterns** - Prevent the docker-lxc module from syncing this directory

# =============================================================================
# Container Management LXC - Pulse + Arcane
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 104
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Container monitoring (Pulse) and management (Arcane).
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 104
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 16
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Container Management LXC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "container_mgmt" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "container-mgmt"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only - no LAN access needed)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.core.container_mgmt}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 512

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Container Management"
  service_description = "Pulse monitoring + Arcane container management"

  service_urls = {
    pulse  = "https://pulse.${var.domain_internal}"
    arcane = "https://arcane.${var.domain_internal}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Pulse", port = 7655, info = "Proxmox + Docker monitoring" },
    { name = "Arcane", port = 3552, info = "Docker container management" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Pulse - Container Monitoring

Real-time monitoring for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
- Dashboard: https://pulse.${var.domain_internal}
- Proxmox metrics via PVE API
- Docker metrics via socket

## Arcane - Container Management

Docker container management with update detection.
- Dashboard: https://arcane.${var.domain_internal}
- Remote agents connect from other LXCs

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f pulse
cd /config && docker compose logs -f arcane
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=container-mgmt` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["pulse", "arcane", "management"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "local_sensitive_file" "container_mgmt_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    pulse_admin_user      = local.op.pulse_admin_user
    pulse_admin_password  = local.op.pulse_admin_password
    arcane_encryption_key = local.op.arcane_encryption_key
    arcane_jwt_secret     = local.op.arcane_jwt_secret
    # Pulse OIDC
    pulse_oidc_issuer        = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/pulse/"
    pulse_oidc_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.pulse.client_id
    pulse_oidc_client_secret = random_password.pulse_oidc_secret.result
    # Arcane OIDC
    arcane_oidc_issuer        = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/arcane/"
    arcane_oidc_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.arcane.client_id
    arcane_oidc_client_secret = random_password.arcane_oidc_secret.result
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/container-mgmt.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "container_mgmt_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.container_mgmt_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.container_mgmt.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "pulse_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "pulse"
  backend_url = "http://${module.container_mgmt.ip_address}:7655"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "pulse.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Pulse uses native OIDC - no forward auth needed
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

module "arcane_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "arcane"
  backend_url = "http://${module.container_mgmt.ip_address}:3552"

  internal_domain = "arcane.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Arcane uses its own auth - native OIDC doesn't persist reliably
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "container_mgmt_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.container_mgmt.container_id
  container_ip   = module.container_mgmt.ip_address
  container_name = "container-mgmt"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00" # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"         # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-104"

    pre_backup_commands = [] # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,container-mgmt"
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    pulse  = module.pulse_route.internal_url
    arcane = module.arcane_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    pulse  = module.pulse_route.remote_config_path
    arcane = module.arcane_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

## llama.cpp Model Management & Web UI Options

### Built-in llama.cpp Features

llama.cpp now has model management capabilities built into llama-server. You can point to a local directory of GGUF files, and on the first request, the server automatically loads the model into memory. Subsequent requests to the same model are instant since it's already loaded.(no content)The server returns all discovered models with their status (loaded, loading, or unloaded), and you can use API endpoints like `/models/load` and `/models/unload` to manage models programmatically.(no content)llama.cpp includes a built-in web UI. You can run a model with a command like `llama-server -m model.gguf --port 8080 --host 127.0.0.1` and access the interface at `http://127.0.0.1:8080`.(no content)With llama-server, you can even download AI models directly from Hugging Face using the `-hf` flag, like `llama-server -hf itlwas/Phi-4-mini-instruct-Q4_K_M-GGUF:Q4_K_M`.

### Third-Party Web UIs

1. **Dan-Duran/llama-cpp-model-controller** - A Flask-based web interface for managing and deploying llama.cpp models. By default, the application looks for models in a `models` directory where you place your GGUF models.

2. **Open WebUI** - Can be integrated with llama.cpp to interact with a locally hosted LLM on your CPU efficiently.(no content)Once configured, Open WebUI will be connected to your locally hosted Llama.cpp model for interacting through the web interface.

3. **text-generation-webui** - Known as the most widely used web UI, this project has numerous features and powerful extensions, and supports GPU acceleration.

4. **KoboldCpp** - A fully featured web UI, with GPU acceleration across all platforms and GPU architectures, especially good for storytelling.

### Downloading GGUF Models

Llama.cpp allows you to download and run inference on a GGUF simply by providing a path to the Hugging Face repo path and the file name. llama.cpp downloads the model checkpoint and automatically caches it.(no content)You can either manually download the GGUF file or directly use any llama.cpp-compatible models from Hugging Face or other model hosting sites by using the CLI argument: `-hf <user>/<model>[:quant]`.

Good news - there are several options:

## Options for Model Management UI

### 1. **llama.cpp Built-in Web UI** (Already available)
The llama-server you're running has a built-in web UI at `http://10.100.5.101:8080`. It can:
- Download models directly from Hugging Face using `-hf` flag
- List and manage loaded models via API

### 2. **[llama-cpp-model-controller](https://github.com/Dan-Duran/llama-cpp-model-controller)** 
A dedicated Flask web UI for managing llama.cpp models - lets you browse, download, and switch models.

### 3. **OpenWebUI Admin Panel**
OpenWebUI itself can manage models if you go to **Admin → Settings → Models**. However, this works better with Ollama than llama.cpp.

### 4. **Hugging Face Direct Download**
llama.cpp supports downloading directly from Hugging Face with the `-hf` flag.

content.text: The llama-server has a built-in web UI. Let me check what model management features it has:

Here are your options:

## Model Management Options

### 1. **llama-server Built-in Web UI** (Already available)
Access it at `https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev` or `http://10.100.5.101:8080`

The UI lets you chat with the model, but doesn't have a download manager built-in.

### 2. **Enable Multi-Model Support with Auto-Discovery**
I can update the llama-server config to scan the `/models` directory for all GGUF files. Then you just need to:
1. Download models to `/tank/llm-models` on Proxmox
2. Restart llama-server (or it auto-detects on API call)

### 3. **[llama-cpp-model-controller](https://github.com/Dan-Duran/llama-cpp-model-controller)** 
A dedicated web UI for downloading and managing models. I could add this as a sidecar container.

### 4. **Use Hugging Face CLI** (Simplest for downloading)
Add `huggingface-cli` to the container and download directly:
```bash
# From Proxmox host
cd /tank/llm-models
curl -L -O "https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/main/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf"
```

---

**My recommendation**: Option 2 (multi-model support) + a simple download script. This keeps things lightweight while letting you easily add models.

Would you like me to:
1. **Enable multi-model scanning** - llama-server will serve any GGUF in `/tank/llm-models`
2. **Add llama-cpp-model-controller** - Full web UI for model management
3. **Keep it simple** - Just use curl/wget to download models manually

Sources:
- [llama.cpp Model Management](https://huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/model-management-in-llamacpp)
- [llama-cpp-model-controller](https://github.com/Dan-Duran/llama-cpp-model-controller)
- [llama.cpp Built-in WebUI Guide](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/16938)

http://10.100.5.101:8080/ is accessible but https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev is not. 
I think we shoould create a script that will help me download models from hugging face using hugging face cli and then if you turn on autodiscovery, that will round off the ease to add new models on llama cpp

# Common Traefik middlewares and transports for homelab
http:
  # ServersTransport for backends with self-signed certificates
  serversTransports:
    insecure:
      insecureSkipVerify: true

  middlewares:
    security-headers:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        forceSTSHeader: true
        stsIncludeSubdomains: true
        stsPreload: true
        stsSeconds: 31536000
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    public-security:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    # Internal-only: Allow only local network, container network, and Tailscale
    internal-only:
      ipAllowList:
        sourceRange:
          - "192.168.1.0/24"    # Local LAN
          - "10.100.0.0/16"     # Container network (LXC containers)
          - "172.16.0.0/12"     # Docker bridge networks (172.16-31.x.x)
          - "100.64.0.0/10"     # Tailscale CGNAT range
          - "127.0.0.1/32"      # Localhost

    # Cloudflare headers - ensures X-Forwarded-Proto: https for public routes
    # This fixes mixed content issues when Cloudflare terminates TLS
    cloudflare-https:
      headers:
        customRequestHeaders:
          X-Forwarded-Proto: "https"
          X-Forwarded-Ssl: "on"

    # llama.cpp API basic auth (OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
    llama-auth:
      basicAuth:
        users:
          - "llama-api:$2y$05$DmLSIME.Uvr6TZEr.qSRK.Nwt9bzfSOV5RXPly9tD8hlQwSGhQz0i"
        realm: "LLaMA API"

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenWebUI - AI Chat Interface
  # ==========================================================================
  openwebui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.6.43
    container_name: openwebui
    environment:
      # Use llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible API instead of Ollama
      - OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://llama-server:8080/v1
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed
      - ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
      - WEBUI_NAME=Homelab AI
      - ENABLE_SIGNUP=false  # Security: Disable public signup
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=llama-3.2-3b-instruct
      # Session secret key (must be persistent)
      - WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=${WEBUI_SECRET_KEY}
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
      - ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP=true
      - OAUTH_MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL=true
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=${OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=${OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - OPENID_PROVIDER_URL=${OPENID_PROVIDER_URL}
      - OAUTH_PROVIDER_NAME=Authentik
      - OAUTH_SCOPES=openid email profile
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./openwebui:/app/backend/data
    depends_on:
      llama-server:
        condition: service_healthy
    # DNS settings for external resolution
    dns:
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 1.1.1.1
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 20480m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 8192m
          cpus: '4.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # llama.cpp Server - LLM Backend (Vulkan GPU Accelerated)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Using Vulkan backend for AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) - provides best
  # performance vs ROCm/CPU. Benchmarked at ~40 tok/s generation,
  # ~800 tok/s prompt processing.
  # ==========================================================================
  llama-server:
    image: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan
    container_name: llama-server
    environment:
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODEL=/models/llama-3.2-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
      - LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE=8192
      - LLAMA_ARG_N_GPU_LAYERS=99
      - LLAMA_ARG_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - LLAMA_ARG_PORT=8080
      # Flash attention for better memory efficiency
      - LLAMA_ARG_FLASH_ATTN=1
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Models stored on ZFS tank (/tank/llm-models) for unlimited storage
      - /llm-models:/models
    # Vulkan GPU passthrough (simpler than ROCm - no /dev/kfd needed)
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 16384m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/health > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# LLM Model Downloader for llama.cpp
# =============================================================================
# Downloads GGUF models from Hugging Face to /llm-models directory.
# Models are automatically discovered by llama-server.
#
# Usage:
#   ./download-model.sh <huggingface-repo> [quantization]
#
# Examples:
#   ./download-model.sh bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF Q4_K_M
#   ./download-model.sh TheBloke/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-GGUF Q5_K_M
#   ./download-model.sh microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-gguf
#
# Popular models:
#   - bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF (3B, fast)
#   - bartowski/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-GGUF (8B, balanced)
#   - TheBloke/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-GGUF (7B, good quality)
#   - microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-gguf (3.8B, efficient)
#   - Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF (7B, multilingual)
#
# Quantization guide (smaller = faster but lower quality):
#   Q2_K   - Smallest, lowest quality
#   Q3_K_M - Very small
#   Q4_K_M - Good balance (recommended)
#   Q5_K_M - Higher quality
#   Q6_K   - Near full quality
#   Q8_0   - Highest quality GGUF
# =============================================================================

set -e

MODELS_DIR="/llm-models"
HF_REPO="${1:-}"
QUANT="${2:-Q4_K_M}"

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 <huggingface-repo> [quantization]"
    echo ""
    echo "Examples:"
    echo "  $0 bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF Q4_K_M"
    echo "  $0 TheBloke/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-GGUF Q5_K_M"
    echo ""
    echo "List current models:"
    echo "  $0 --list"
    echo ""
    echo "Search Hugging Face:"
    echo "  $0 --search <query>"
    exit 1
}

list_models() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Models in ${MODELS_DIR}:${NC}"
    echo ""
    if [ -d "$MODELS_DIR" ]; then
        ls -lh "$MODELS_DIR"/*.gguf 2>/dev/null || echo "No models found"
    else
        echo "Models directory not found: $MODELS_DIR"
    fi
    echo ""
    echo -e "${YELLOW}To check loaded models via API:${NC}"
    echo "  curl http://localhost:8080/v1/models"
}

search_models() {
    local query="$1"
    echo -e "${GREEN}Searching Hugging Face for: ${query}${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo "Opening browser..."
    echo "https://huggingface.co/models?search=${query}&library=gguf"
    echo ""
    echo "Popular GGUF model providers:"
    echo "  - bartowski (high quality quants)"
    echo "  - TheBloke (wide variety)"
    echo "  - Qwen (official Qwen models)"
    echo "  - microsoft (Phi models)"
}

download_model() {
    local repo="$1"
    local quant="$2"

    echo -e "${GREEN}Downloading model from: ${repo}${NC}"
    echo -e "Quantization: ${quant}"
    echo ""

    # Check if huggingface-cli is available
    if command -v huggingface-cli &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Using huggingface-cli..."
        cd "$MODELS_DIR"

        # Try to find the file matching the quantization
        local filename=$(huggingface-cli download "$repo" --include "*${quant}*.gguf" --local-dir . 2>&1 | grep -o '[^ ]*\.gguf' | head -1)

        if [ -n "$filename" ]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}Downloaded: ${filename}${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}Trying direct download...${NC}"
            huggingface-cli download "$repo" --include "*.gguf" --local-dir .
        fi
    else
        echo "huggingface-cli not found, using curl..."

        # Construct download URL
        # Format: https://huggingface.co/{repo}/resolve/main/{filename}
        local base_url="https://huggingface.co/${repo}/resolve/main"

        # Try to find the correct filename
        echo "Fetching file list..."
        local files=$(curl -sL "https://huggingface.co/api/models/${repo}/tree/main" | grep -o '"path":"[^"]*\.gguf"' | sed 's/"path":"//g;s/"//g')

        if [ -z "$files" ]; then
            echo -e "${RED}Could not find GGUF files in repository${NC}"
            echo "Please check the repository URL and try again"
            exit 1
        fi

        # Find file matching quantization
        local target_file=$(echo "$files" | grep -i "$quant" | head -1)

        if [ -z "$target_file" ]; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}No file matching '${quant}' found. Available files:${NC}"
            echo "$files"
            echo ""
            echo "Please specify the exact filename or choose a quantization from above"
            exit 1
        fi

        echo -e "Downloading: ${target_file}"
        cd "$MODELS_DIR"
        curl -L -O "${base_url}/${target_file}" --progress-bar

        echo -e "${GREEN}Downloaded: ${target_file}${NC}"
    fi

    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}Model downloaded successfully!${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo "The model will be available after restarting llama-server:"
    echo "  cd /config && docker compose restart llama-server"
    echo ""
    echo "Or call the API to load it:"
    echo "  curl http://localhost:8080/v1/models"
}

# Main
case "$HF_REPO" in
    "")
        usage
        ;;
    "--list"|"-l")
        list_models
        ;;
    "--search"|"-s")
        search_models "$2"
        ;;
    "--help"|"-h")
        usage
        ;;
    *)
        download_model "$HF_REPO" "$QUANT"
        ;;
esac

#
# Benchmarked performance (Vulkan vs ROCm vs CPU):
#   - Vulkan: ~800 tok/s prompt, ~40 tok/s generation (WINNER)
#   - ROCm:   ~30 tok/s prompt,  ~29 tok/s generation
#   - CPU:    ~28 tok/s prompt,  ~28 tok/s generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Mount points - LLM models on ZFS tank for unlimited storage
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/llm-models"
      volume = "/tank/llm-models"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with llama.cpp backend (Vulkan GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "llama-server", port = 8080, info = "LLM backend (Vulkan GPU)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) via Vulkan/RADV:
- `/dev/dri` device passthrough
- ~40 tok/s generation, ~800 tok/s prompt processing

**Check GPU detection:**
```
docker logs llama-server 2>&1 | grep -i vulkan
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f llama-server
```

**Test inference:**
```
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3.2-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```

**Download new model (GGUF format):**
```
cd /llm-models
curl -L -O "https://huggingface.co/bartowski/MODEL/resolve/main/MODEL.gguf"
```

Models are stored on ZFS tank (`/tank/llm-models` → `/llm-models`).

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "llama-cpp", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "openwebui_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    webui_secret_key    = random_password.openwebui_secret_key.result
    oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.openwebui.client_id
    oauth_client_secret = random_password.openwebui_oidc_secret.result
    openid_provider_url = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/openwebui/.well-known/openid-configuration"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/openwebui.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "openwebui_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.openwebui_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.openwebui.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.openwebui.container_id
  container_ip   = module.openwebui.ip_address
  container_name = "openwebui"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-501"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database dump needed - SQLite file backup is sufficient

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]  # Models are on /tank, not backed up here

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,openwebui"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenWebUI (AI Chat Interface)
module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal and public routes (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "ai.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# llama.cpp API (LLM Backend - OpenAI compatible)
module "llama_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "llama"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal only (OpenAI-compatible API access)
  internal_domain = "llama.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Basic auth for API access
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "llama-auth"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    openwebui = {
      internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
      public   = module.openwebui_route.public_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
    }
    llama = {
      internal = module.llama_route.internal_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"
    }
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    openwebui = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
    llama     = module.llama_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

# Homelab Infrastructure Automation
# https://taskfile.dev

version: '3'

vars:
  PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.TASKFILE_DIR}}"
  TOFU_DIR: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/tofu"

env:
  # State encryption passphrase - MUST be TF_VAR because encryption runs before providers
  # All other secrets are now fetched via 1Password provider directly in OpenTofu
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: |
      if [ -n "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase" ]; then
        echo "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase"
      else
        op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password" 2>/dev/null || echo ""
      fi
  # SOPS age key for decrypting secrets (used by sops provider in OpenTofu)
  SOPS_AGE_KEY:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/sops-age-key/private_key" 2>/dev/null || echo ""
  # DNS mode: 'home' (LAN 192.168.1.x) or 'travel' (Tailscale 10.100.x.x)
  # Set to 'travel' when working remotely via Tailscale
  TF_VAR_dns_mode: travel

# =============================================================================
# Included Taskfiles (flattened into main namespace)
# =============================================================================
includes:
  tofu:
    taskfile: ./tasks/tofu.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  cloud:
    taskfile: ./tasks/cloud.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  template:
    taskfile: ./tasks/template.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  pbs:
    taskfile: ./tasks/pbs.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  importer:
    taskfile: ./tasks/immich-importer.yml
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  beads:
    taskfile: ./tasks/beads.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"

tasks:
  # ===========================================================================
  # Desktop LXC (Temporary GUI for Downloads)
  # ===========================================================================

  desktop:create:
    desc: "Create temporary GUI desktop LXC for downloading Google Takeout"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/create.sh

  desktop:destroy:
    desc: "Destroy temporary GUI desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/destroy.sh

  desktop:info:
    desc: "Show VNC connection info for desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        IP=$(ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet | awk '{print \$2}' | cut -d/ -f1" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -z "$IP" ]; then
          echo "Desktop LXC (600) is not running or does not exist."
          echo "Run 'task desktop:create' first."
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "=== Desktop LXC VNC Connection ==="
        echo ""
        echo "VNC Host: $IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "macOS: Open Finder, Cmd+K, enter vnc://$IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "Downloads save to: /downloads (mounted to /tank/photo-import)"

  desktop:restart-vnc:
    desc: "Restart VNC server on desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "Restarting VNC server..."
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- bash -c 'vncserver -kill :1 2>/dev/null || true; vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no'"
        echo "VNC server restarted on display :1"

# Homelab Infrastructure Automation
# https://taskfile.dev

version: '3'

vars:
  PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.TASKFILE_DIR}}"
  TOFU_DIR: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/tofu"

env:
  # State encryption passphrase - MUST be TF_VAR because encryption runs before providers
  # All other secrets are now fetched via 1Password provider directly in OpenTofu
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: |
      if [ -n "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase" ]; then
        echo "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase"
      else
        op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password" 2>/dev/null || echo ""
      fi
  # SOPS age key for decrypting secrets (used by sops provider in OpenTofu)
  SOPS_AGE_KEY:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/sops-age-key/private_key" 2>/dev/null || echo ""
  # DNS mode: 'home' (LAN 192.168.1.x) or 'travel' (Tailscale 10.100.x.x)
  # Set to 'travel' when working remotely via Tailscale
  TF_VAR_dns_mode: travel

# =============================================================================
# Included Taskfiles (flattened into main namespace)
# =============================================================================
includes:
  tofu:
    taskfile: ./tasks/tofu.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  cloud:
    taskfile: ./tasks/cloud.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  template:
    taskfile: ./tasks/template.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  pbs:
    taskfile: ./tasks/pbs.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  importer:
    taskfile: ./tasks/immich-importer.yml
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  beads:
    taskfile: ./tasks/beads.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"

tasks:
  # ===========================================================================
  # Desktop LXC (Temporary GUI for Downloads)
  # ===========================================================================

  desktop:create:
    desc: "Create temporary GUI desktop LXC for downloading Google Takeout"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/create.sh

  desktop:destroy:
    desc: "Destroy temporary GUI desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/destroy.sh

  desktop:info:
    desc: "Show VNC connection info for desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        IP=$(ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet | awk '{print \$2}' | cut -d/ -f1" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -z "$IP" ]; then
          echo "Desktop LXC (600) is not running or does not exist."
          echo "Run 'task desktop:create' first."
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "=== Desktop LXC VNC Connection ==="
        echo ""
        echo "VNC Host: $IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "macOS: Open Finder, Cmd+K, enter vnc://$IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "Downloads save to: /downloads (mounted to /tank/photo-import)"

  desktop:restart-vnc:
    desc: "Restart VNC server on desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "Restarting VNC server..."
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- bash -c 'vncserver -kill :1 2>/dev/null || true; vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no'"
        echo "VNC server restarted on display :1"

  # ===========================================================================
  # AdGuard DNS Operations
  # ===========================================================================

  adguard:test:
    desc: "Test DNS resolution for homelab domains"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/sync/adguard-sync.sh test

  # ===========================================================================
  # Cleanup & Maintenance
  # ===========================================================================

  cleanup:
    desc: "Clean up temporary files, backups, and cruft (dry run)"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/cleanup.sh

  cleanup:run:
    desc: "Clean up temporary files, backups, and cruft (actually delete)"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/cleanup.sh --run

  # ===========================================================================
  # Local Development
  # ===========================================================================

  dev:dashboards:up:
    desc: "Start Homepage and Dashy locally for testing configs"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose up -d
      - |
        echo ""
        echo "=== Dashboard Dev Environment ==="
        echo ""
        echo "Homepage: http://localhost:3000"
        echo "Dashy:    http://localhost:4001"
        echo ""
        echo "Config files are mounted from tofu/apps/dashboards/deploy/"
        echo "Edit configs and refresh browser to see changes."
        echo "(Dashy may need container restart for config changes)"
        echo ""
        echo "Stop with: task dev:dashboards:down"

  dev:dashboards:down:
    desc: "Stop local dashboard dev environment"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose down

  dev:dashboards:logs:
    desc: "View logs from local dashboard containers"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose logs -f {{.SERVICE}}
    vars:
      SERVICE: '{{.SERVICE | default ""}}'

  dev:dashboards:restart:
    desc: "Restart local dashboard containers (useful after config changes)"
    dir: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/dev/dashboards"
    cmds:
      - docker compose restart {{.SERVICE}}
      - echo "Restarted. Dashy takes ~40s to fully start."
    vars:
      SERVICE: '{{.SERVICE | default ""}}'

Analysis:
Let me analyze this conversation chronologically to capture all the technical details:

## Session Start (Continuation)
This session is a continuation from a previous conversation. The summary indicated the user migrated from Ollama to llama.cpp with Vulkan GPU acceleration for their OpenWebUI setup.

## Key Work Done Previously:
- Replaced Ollama with llama.cpp Vulkan backend
- Added ZFS mount (`/tank/llm-models` → `/llm-models`) for model storage
- Updated Traefik middleware from `ollama-auth` to `llama-auth`
- Cleaned up 12GB of old Ollama models
- Removed old `ollama.yml` Traefik route

## Current Session Messages:

1. **User**: "i dont think openwebui is connecting to llama.cpp"
   - I checked containers, logs, and verified the API connection was working
   - OpenWebUI env vars were correctly set
   - Suggested checking admin panel settings since database overrides env vars

2. **User**: "and what about other apps like n8n or pulse"
   - Checked for Ollama references in codebase
   - Found Pulse mentions Ollama in comments but isn't configured for it
   - n8n has no LLM workflows configured
   - Explained connection details for llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible API

3. **User**: "they are not connected yet" / "how do i connect?"
   - Provided instructions for configuring OpenWebUI via Admin Panel
   - Explained n8n credential setup with OpenAI API node

4. **User**: "do we expose this to traefik?"
   - Confirmed llama.cpp is already exposed via `llama_route` module
   - URL: `https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev/v1` with basic auth

5. **User**: "we need to sync up the tofu/apps/container-mgmt/deploy/pulse directory with whats in the actual pulse volumes"
   - Found local deploy/pulse had stale data from Dec 20
   - Container had current runtime data

6. **User**: "actually lets cleanup the local deploy/pulse directory"
   - Removed local `deploy/pulse` directory
   - Added `exclude_patterns = ["pulse/**", "arcane_data/**"]` to container-mgmt main.tf

7. **User**: "is there any UI I can use that will help me download new models to the right place and load it with llama cpp?"
   - Researched model management options
   - Found llama-server has built-in web UI and `--models-dir` for auto-discovery
   - Found `--hf` flag for Hugging Face downloads
   - Recommended enabling multi-model support + download script

8. **User**: "http://10.100.5.101:8080/ is accessible but https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev is not. I think we should create a script that will help me download models from hugging face using hugging face cli and then if you turn on autodiscovery, that will round off the ease to add new models on llama cpp"
   - Found Traefik route was disabled due to missing `llama-auth` middleware
   - Applied Traefik config to sync common.yml with llama-auth
   - Fixed the route - now working with correct password from 1Password (`ollama-api`)
   - Updated docker-compose.yml to add `LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_DIR=/models` for auto-discovery
   - Created `download-model.sh` script with list, search, and download functionality
   - Applied OpenWebUI terraform changes

9. **User**: "lets create a task cmd to run that script. then apply the terraform changes and download a test model. only then we should commit"
   - Added LLM task commands to Taskfile.yml:
     - `llm:list` - List models
     - `llm:download` - Download from HuggingFace
     - `llm:models` - Show API models
     - `llm:restart` - Restart llama-server
   - Ran `task tofu:plan APP=openwebui` - got error about file_permissions needing absolute path

## Error Encountered:
The `file_permissions` variable in main.tf was set incorrectly:
```hcl
file_permissions = {
  "download-model.sh" = "0755"
}
```
But the module expects absolute paths. Error: "Path must be an absolute path starting with '/'"

## Files Modified:

1. **tofu/apps/container-mgmt/main.tf** - Added exclude_patterns
2. **tofu/apps/openwebui/deploy/docker-compose.yml** - Added LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_DIR
3. **tofu/apps/openwebui/main.tf** - Added file_permissions (has error)
4. **tofu/apps/openwebui/deploy/download-model.sh** - Created new script
5. **Taskfile.yml** - Added llm:* tasks

## Pending:
- Fix file_permissions error (needs absolute path)
- Apply terraform changes
- Download a test model
- Commit all changes

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user wanted to enhance the llama.cpp setup (migrated from Ollama in previous session) with:
   - A UI/script to download new GGUF models from Hugging Face
   - Multi-model auto-discovery so llama-server can serve any model in the `/models` directory
   - Task commands to easily manage models from the command line
   - Fix the Traefik route for `https://llama.homelab.rambtech.dev`

   - OpenAI-compatible API (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`)

# =============================================================================
# OpenWebUI LXC - AI Chat Interface with llama.cpp
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 501
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Features Vulkan GPU acceleration for llama.cpp (AMD Radeon 890M gfx1150).
#
# Benchmarked performance (Vulkan vs ROCm vs CPU):
#   - Vulkan: ~800 tok/s prompt, ~40 tok/s generation (WINNER)
#   - ROCm:   ~30 tok/s prompt,  ~29 tok/s generation
#   - CPU:    ~28 tok/s prompt,  ~28 tok/s generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Mount points - LLM models on ZFS tank for unlimited storage
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/llm-models"
      volume = "/tank/llm-models"
    }
  ]

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Make download script executable
  file_permissions = {
    "download-model.sh" = "0755"
  }

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = local.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with llama.cpp backend (Vulkan GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "llama-server", port = 8080, info = "LLM backend (Vulkan GPU)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) via Vulkan/RADV:
- `/dev/dri` device passthrough
- ~40 tok/s generation, ~800 tok/s prompt processing

**Check GPU detection:**
```
docker logs llama-server 2>&1 | grep -i vulkan
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f llama-server
```

**Test inference:**
```
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3.2-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```

**Download new model (GGUF format):**
```
cd /llm-models
curl -L -O "https://huggingface.co/bartowski/MODEL/resolve/main/MODEL.gguf"
```

Models are stored on ZFS tank (`/tank/llm-models` → `/llm-models`).

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "llama-cpp", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "openwebui_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    webui_secret_key    = random_password.openwebui_secret_key.result
    oauth_client_id     = authentik_provider_oauth2.openwebui.client_id
    oauth_client_secret = random_password.openwebui_oidc_secret.result
    openid_provider_url = "https://auth.${var.domain_public}/application/o/openwebui/.well-known/openid-configuration"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/openwebui.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "openwebui_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.openwebui_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.openwebui.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.openwebui.container_id
  container_ip   = module.openwebui.ip_address
  container_name = "openwebui"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = local.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-501"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database dump needed - SQLite file backup is sufficient

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]  # Models are on /tank, not backed up here

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,openwebui"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenWebUI (AI Chat Interface)
module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal and public routes (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "ai.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# llama.cpp API (LLM Backend - OpenAI compatible)
module "llama_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "llama"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal only (OpenAI-compatible API access)
  internal_domain = "llama.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Basic auth for API access
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "llama-auth"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    openwebui = {
      internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
      public   = module.openwebui_route.public_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
    }
    llama = {
      internal = module.llama_route.internal_url
      direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:8080"
    }
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    openwebui = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
    llama     = module.llama_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenWebUI - AI Chat Interface
  # ==========================================================================
  openwebui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.6.43
    container_name: openwebui
    environment:
      # Use llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible API instead of Ollama
      - OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://llama-server:8080/v1
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed
      - ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
      - WEBUI_NAME=Homelab AI
      - ENABLE_SIGNUP=false  # Security: Disable public signup
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=llama-3.2-3b-instruct
      # Session secret key (must be persistent)
      - WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=${WEBUI_SECRET_KEY}
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
      - ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP=true
      - OAUTH_MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL=true
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=${OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=${OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - OPENID_PROVIDER_URL=${OPENID_PROVIDER_URL}
      - OAUTH_PROVIDER_NAME=Authentik
      - OAUTH_SCOPES=openid email profile
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./openwebui:/app/backend/data
    depends_on:
      llama-server:
        condition: service_healthy
    # DNS settings for external resolution
    dns:
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 1.1.1.1
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 20480m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 8192m
          cpus: '4.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # llama.cpp Server - LLM Backend (Vulkan GPU Accelerated)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Using Vulkan backend for AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) - provides best
  # performance vs ROCm/CPU. Benchmarked at ~40 tok/s generation,
  # ~800 tok/s prompt processing.
  # ==========================================================================
  llama-server:
    image: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan
    container_name: llama-server
    environment:
      # Multi-model support: scans /models directory for all GGUF files
      # Models are loaded on-demand when requested via API
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_DIR=/models
      # Default model to load at startup (for health checks)
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODEL=/models/llama-3.2-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
      - LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE=8192
      - LLAMA_ARG_N_GPU_LAYERS=99
      - LLAMA_ARG_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - LLAMA_ARG_PORT=8080
      # Flash attention for better memory efficiency
      - LLAMA_ARG_FLASH_ATTN=1
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Models stored on ZFS tank (/tank/llm-models) for unlimited storage
      - /llm-models:/models
    # Vulkan GPU passthrough (simpler than ROCm - no /dev/kfd needed)
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 16384m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/health > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenWebUI - AI Chat Interface
  # ==========================================================================
  openwebui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.6.43
    container_name: openwebui
    environment:
      # Use llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible API instead of Ollama
      - OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://llama-server:8080/v1
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed
      - ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
      - WEBUI_NAME=Homelab AI
      - ENABLE_SIGNUP=false  # Security: Disable public signup
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=llama-3.2-3b-instruct
      # Session secret key (must be persistent)
      - WEBUI_SECRET_KEY=${WEBUI_SECRET_KEY}
      # OAuth/OIDC via Authentik
      - ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP=true
      - OAUTH_MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL=true
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=${OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      - OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=${OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - OPENID_PROVIDER_URL=${OPENID_PROVIDER_URL}
      - OAUTH_PROVIDER_NAME=Authentik
      - OAUTH_SCOPES=openid email profile
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./openwebui:/app/backend/data
    depends_on:
      llama-server:
        condition: service_healthy
    # DNS settings for external resolution
    dns:
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 1.1.1.1
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 20480m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 8192m
          cpus: '4.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # llama.cpp Server - LLM Backend (Vulkan GPU Accelerated)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Using Vulkan backend for AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) - provides best
  # performance vs ROCm/CPU. Benchmarked at ~40 tok/s generation,
  # ~800 tok/s prompt processing.
  # ==========================================================================
  llama-server:
    image: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan
    container_name: llama-server
    environment:
      # Multi-model support: scans /models directory for all GGUF files
      # Models are loaded on-demand when requested via API
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODELS_DIR=/models
      # Default model to load at startup (for health checks)
      - LLAMA_ARG_MODEL=/models/llama-3.2-3b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
      - LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE=8192
      - LLAMA_ARG_N_GPU_LAYERS=99
      - LLAMA_ARG_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - LLAMA_ARG_PORT=8080
      # Flash attention for better memory efficiency
      - LLAMA_ARG_FLASH_ATTN=1
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      # Models stored on ZFS tank (/tank/llm-models) for unlimited storage
      - /llm-models:/models
    # Vulkan GPU passthrough (simpler than ROCm - no /dev/kfd needed)
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 16384m
          cpus: '8.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:8080/health > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
